D006-D010_h001.question:
It’s been a confusing year. Around ten months ago my wife started saying I was “amped up all the time.” I’ve been snapping at my students and colleagues over tiny things, getting unreasonably angry if someone questions my ideas. At home I’m pacing, talking fast, starting three or four new research projects at once, reorganizing the whole syllabus, then abandoning it halfway through because another “brilliant” idea hits. I barely finish anything. It’s really disrupted my teaching; I missed deadlines, stopped answering emails.

For about eight months I’ve also had these…odd experiences. I feel things crawling across my skin or like someone is brushing past me when I’m alone in my office. I’ve become convinced people at the university are watching me, tracking my computer, maybe even planting devices. I’ve even started using words my wife says don’t exist—“mind‑tuning,” “data‑shadowing”—but they make sense to me.

What frightens me is that even during a three‑month stretch when my mood crashed—barely leaving bed, ignoring friends, wishing I wouldn’t wake up—the sensations on my skin and the feeling of being monitored kept going. And there were at least a couple of weeks between the high and the low when my mood felt more or less normal, but the crawling sensations and conviction of being watched were still there.
D006-D010_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder

D006-D010_h002.question:

About 8 months ago I started seeing things that aren’t there. I’ll see shadowy figures in the bay, or people standing at the end of the bunk room, watching me. Sometimes at home I’m convinced there are men in unmarked trucks following me, monitoring my radio calls and our dispatch system. I know it sounds crazy, but it feels real.

A few months back, I crashed hard for about 3 months—stopped going to the gym, didn’t care about anything, even thought about ending it and started collecting my pain pills. The strange visions and feeling watched kept going then, even when that “high” mood was completely gone and I could barely get off the couch.
D006-D010_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Delusional Disorder
